market_holds: Spot $55.33 at 18:08 UTC (sealed baseline), and the last daily bar reads $54.51. The 20-session run-up is -23.9% and the 5-session -2.1%. The front-expiry straddle implies 14.4%, or about 10.0% for the event net of ordinary vol. The 25-delta skew is +2.9 vol points, so downside is paid, and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.73. The seven prior reactions had a median of 5.1% and a maximum of 17.75% (Nov 2025, a guide cut on server shortages). The run-in is mostly tape. Measured on my own Yahoo bars from 10-28 to 11-24: NTNX -25.0%, IGV -14.4%, QQQ -11.9%. The hardware complex it trades beside fell further: DELL about -40%, HPE about -33%, NTAP -27%. That came with the AI/tech rout (Nasdaq 100 -6.4% on 11-05) and memory-cost fears, including NTNX -4.2% on 10-14 when Dell fell 11% on memory concerns. Consensus as of 2026-11-16 (Earnings Whispers via Finviz) is revenue $761.8M, slightly above the $755-765M guide midpoint, and non-GAAP EPS $0.60, with a whisper of $0.71. The FY27 guide of $3.18-3.23B, set 2026-08-26, already assumes server/CPU/memory constraints through all of FY27, a higher mix of future-start-date deals, and slower renewals. Short interest is about 12M shares, 4-6% of float, edging up (equibles, as of 11-13). That is not crowded. The stock trades on the guide (the Nov 2025 -17.75% came on the Q2 outlook and an FY cut).
view: Since the Nov 2025 reset, Nutanix has guided revenue conservatively and then beaten the top of its range three times in a row: Q2 $722.8M vs a $715M high end, Q3 $703M vs $690M, Q4 $757.1M vs $745M. That is 1.1-1.9% above the high end each time. The Q1 FY27 guide midpoint of $760M is only +0.4% over Q4's $757.1M, while last year's Q4-to-Q1 step was about +2.7% even in the quarter that disappointed (my arithmetic from the cited growth rates). So a revenue print around $770-775M and a large EPS beat (Q4 operating margin 26.2% vs a 21-23% guide, plus layoff savings) are the base case. The deciding line is whether the FY27 guide holds or rises. The risk to it is the one that broke the stock a year ago: server and CPU shortages and price rises pushing licence start dates out. Inputs since the last call point both ways. DRAM contract prices hit a record in October 2026, and Q4 DRAM is forecast +10-15% QoQ (TrendForce, 2026-09-30). HPE said today that memory and NAND stay constrained into H2 2028 and price increases were steep through 2026. But Nutanix already guided FY27 on exactly that assumption. HPE's traditional server orders grew strong double digits with units supply-limited, and Cisco's enterprise data-centre switching orders were up about 40% (reported 2026-11-12). So enterprise infrastructure demand is intact. A softer signal: the President and Chief Commercial Officer stepped down effective 2026-10-02, four weeks before the quarter closed. The stock shrugged that off. The stock has fallen about 10 points more than software, alongside the hardware complex, so the bar is lower than in August. A held or slightly raised FY guide with a beat should get a relief open, while an FY trim reprises the Nov 2025 tail. I lean modestly up, but the overnight window also carries Dell's own print tonight and a tape where QQQ has had several moves of 5% or more in a day. Not a bet.
unpriced: Possibly a modest one. Sell-side revenue consensus sits at the guide midpoint despite three straight beats of the high end. The 25% drawdown came mostly with the tech/hardware tape rather than Nutanix-specific news, so it may overstate the guide-cut risk the company already built into FY27. But the buy-side whisper ($0.71 vs $0.60) shows a beat is expected. The guide line cannot be seen, and its main input (server supply) moved against the company within the quarter. So I cannot show the price is behind by enough to act.

recommendation.reason: A beat of the revenue range and of EPS is likely given the guide pattern since the reset, and the stock has de-rated with the tape. But the reaction turns on the FY27 guide. Its main input, server and memory availability and price, worsened during the quarter (DRAM record in October, HPE calling supply tight into 2028), and the CCO left four weeks before quarter end. My probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 revenue guide below $3.18-3.23B, or Q2 guided materially under about $790M with commentary on more future-start-date deals. That is the Nov 2025 pattern and would take the open sharply lower.

self_critique: The 10-point lag against software may not be beta. It could be informed money pricing a repeat of Nov 2025: Q1 is the quarter where the hardware squeeze first hit last year, DRAM and CPU conditions tightened through the quarter, and the chief commercial officer left four weeks before it closed. If future-start-date deals rose more than the August guide assumed, Nutanix might beat Q1 but hold or trim FY27, and the market has punished that hard (-8.2 and -12.7 opens). Even beat-and-raise prints have opened flat or negative (May 2026 -1.2). The whisper already expects a beat. Overnight, Dell's print tonight and a tape making 5% index moves can swamp the company signal. These keep me from going above the high 50s. Nothing here argues for a number below 50, so I leave p_up at 57.
